demos.description:
LAMP WITH A HIDDEN FAULT, PARTIALLY OBSERVABLE

One agent, R, must get the lamp running. The lamp may have a fault.

Skills (one skill per decision cycle):
  Start(agent, lamp): try to start the lamp. A faulty lamp never starts, and even a
    healthy one sometimes fails to start. The status is ok if the lamp is running afterwards.
  Inspect(agent, lamp): look the lamp over. The reading (looks_faulty | looks_fine) is
    usually, but not always, right about whether it is faulty. Status ok.
  Repair(agent, lamp): work on the stopped lamp. Repairing sometimes clears a fault and
    never causes one. Status ok whenever the repair was carried out.

Hidden: whether the lamp is faulty is decided at random at the start and never shown directly.

Observed after every skill: whether the lamp is running, the skill's status (ok | fail), and after Inspect the reading.

Rewards: -0.01 per cycle, an extra -0.05 per repair, +1 when the lamp runs. Discount 0.95.

The probabilities are NOT given: model each one as a named parameter.

CHEST WITH A STICKY LID, PARTIALLY OBSERVABLE

One agent, R, must open the chest.

Skills (one skill per decision cycle):
  OpenLid(agent, chest): lift the closed lid. A stuck lid never opens. Even a free lid sometimes does not come up.
    The status is ok if the lid is open afterwards.
  Tap(agent, chest): tap the closed lid. Tapping sometimes frees a stuck lid and never sticks a free
    one. Status ok whenever the tap was made.
    The agent then hears a sound (thud | click) that usually, but not always, tells whether the
    lid is still stuck afterwards.

Hidden: whether the lid starts stuck is decided at random and never shown directly.

Observed after every skill: whether the lid is open, the skill's status (ok | fail), and after Tap the sound.

Rewards: -0.02 per cycle, an extra -0.1 per tap, +2 when the chest is open. Discount 0.9.

The probabilities are NOT given: model each one as a named parameter.

VAULT BEHIND A DOOR THAT MAY BE LOCKED, PARTIALLY OBSERVABLE

Two agents, P and Q, start in the corridor. Rooms hall_a and hall_b lie along it, and the vault lies behind a door
that opens from hall_b. The task succeeds when both agents are in the vault.

Skills (one skill per decision cycle):
  Goto(agent, room), room in {hall_a, hall_b}: walk to a room. A room holds one agent at
    a time, and an agent never goes to the room it is already in.
    The passage is one person wide: P cannot get past Q into hall_b while Q is in hall_a;
    such a Goto fails and the agent stays.
  EnterVault(agent, door): from hall_b, step through the door into the vault. A locked door
    refuses entry and the agent stays. An agent in the vault stays there.
  Unlock(agent, door): from hall_b, unlock the door with the key; afterwards it is certainly
    unlocked. Status ok.
  Knock(agent, door): from hall_b, knock on the door. The echo (dull | hollow) is usually, but
    not always, dull when the door is locked and hollow when it is not. Status ok.

Hidden: whether the door starts locked is decided at random and never shown directly.

Observed after every skill: where each agent is (a room, the vault, or the corridor), the skill's
status (ok | fail), and after Knock the echo.

Rewards: -0.05 per agent per cycle, an extra -0.02 per unlock, +5 per agent when both are in the vault. Discount 0.98.

The probabilities are NOT given: model each one as a named parameter.

signature.instructions:
You are a POMDP modeling engineer. Convert the ENVIRONMENT DESCRIPTION below into a factored
POMDP model written ONLY as one JSON object {"domain": {...}, "problem": {...}} in the MAAOS
skill-IR format. A deterministic compiler (not you) turns it into tables for a POMDP solver, and
a statistical fitter (not you) estimates every probability from data. YOUR JOB IS STRUCTURE.

FORMAT RULES
F1  domain keys: name, model_version, types, constants, parameters, observation_channels,
    predicates, skills, provenance. problem keys: name, domain, objects, init, hidden_prior,
    goal, rewards, discount.
F2  Every object you mention is a constant {"name","type"} with a declared type.
F3  Predicates are boolean: {"name","param_types","fluent"} plus "observable": false for a
    variable that is never shown. fluent=false means the value never changes.
F4  A skill has "name", "parameters" (names), "parameter_types" (parallel types),
    "preconditions" and optional "negative_preconditions" (lists of {"name","args"}), and either
    plain "effects" (one certain outcome) or "outcomes": [{"label","effects"}] with
    "outcome_label" naming the outcome a planner should hope for. An effect is
    {"predicate": {"name","args"}, "positive": true|false}. Args are parameter names or constants.
F5  "*" as an argument is allowed ONLY in a negative precondition (no grounding holds) or a
    negative effect (delete every grounding), e.g. not at(agent, *) before adding at(agent, place).
F6  Hidden (observable=false) predicates must NEVER appear in preconditions. They may appear in
    outcome cases, effects and observation cases.
F7  With two or more outcomes, give "outcome_cases": a decision list
    [{"when": [atoms], "distribution": D}], first match wins, the LAST case has "when": [].
    An atom is {"literal": {"name","args"}, "positive": bool} or {"equals": [parameter, constant]}.
F8  D is {"deterministic": label} or
    {"bernoulli": {"p": {"parameter": name}, "then": label1, "else": label2}}.
    Every probability you were not given is a NAMED PARAMETER declared in "parameters" as
    {"name": ..., "prior": {"beta": ["1", "1"]}}. Never write a number for it.
F9  "observation_channels": [{"name", "symbols"}]; the first symbol is "none". A skill's
    "observation_cases" is an object {channel: decision list}; conditions are read on the state
    AFTER the skill. Positions and other observable predicates are observed automatically.
F10 problem: "init" = observable ground literals true at the start (static ones included);
    "hidden_prior" = [{"literal": {"name","args"}, "p": {"parameter": name}}];
    "goal" = ground literals; "rewards" = {"step": r, "skills": {skill: extra}, "goal": r} as
    exact fraction strings such as "-1/50"; "discount" as a fraction string.
F11 Use exactly the skill names and parameters given in the description. Output ONLY the JSON.

fields.description: the environment description, the sole input
one JSON object {"domain": {...}, "problem": {...}} in the MAAOS skill-IR format, nothing else
